flagship_directive: Complete the support-scoped compiler by proving finite termination and rule-by-rule soundness and completeness relative to the tensor criterion, with an explicit certificate-size bound and reproducible implementation benchmarks.
critique: The note proves a complete formula-or-twins characterization only for the canonical independent-district-root class Theta_S; broader finite-SCM classes receive necessity alone, exactly as the framing states. The advertised support-scoped do-search compiler is not delivered, so the semantic tensor test still requires potentially enormous response-space matrices and has no termination, complexity, or certificate-size guarantee. The novelty case needs a theorem-level comparison with Zaffalon et al. (2020), whose Theorem 2 already gives exact rootwise credal representations for quasi-Markovian models, to establish that support saturation and the symbolic row-span dichotomy are not consequences of that representation. The presolve enumeration and software evidence are absent from the delivered note, leaving only two hand-worked controls and weakening reproducibility and practical significance. The variance estimator is undefined on empirical boundary events as stated, and the invoked Lindeberg–Feller theorem lacks a precise citation; these are repairable presentation defects but further constrain journal readiness.
